subject: Renewal: Surgeproof sizing, observability checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@novamed.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Mar 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: Surgeproof sizing, observability checklist & next steps

Hi Elena —

Thanks for taking time last week to walk through NovaMed's March runway. Attached is a focused sizing worksheet (surgeproof-sizing-worksheet.xlsx) and a short observability checklist that ties metrics we use for dedicated sizing decisions to contract options. High level observations from your Feb usage CSV: average utilization across inference GPUs was ~62% but P95 token latency spikes aligned with model cold starts and long-context bursts. That pattern predicts a good candidate for a small dedicated buffer + 15% burst tranche rather than a straight tranche increase.

Why I'm suggesting this: a smoothing buffer (reserved) + burst tranche (on-demand reserved credits) tends to keep unit costs reasonable while preventing client-facing tail latencies during unexpected surges. Key levers we propose: continuous KV prefix caching, a short-lived burst pool (30–90s), and a canary rollout to a 6 GPU dedicated pool (quantized variant) before switching full traffic.

Request: can you confirm (1) if Procurement needs an updated T&C for burst credits vs. reserved commit, (2) whether NovaMed can share two additional 24-hour traces (Mar 1–2) so we can validate the cache-hit model, and (3) who should sign the SOW?

I've penciled three next steps in the attached checklist and linked the HubSpot playbook for the renewal (DEAL-14829). If it helps, Ben can run a quick sim on our testbed with your traces and return a P95/P99 forecast within 48 hours.

Thanks —
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
attachments: novamed_feb_usage_summary.csv (csv), surgeproof-sizing-worksheet.xlsx (xlsx), observability-checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Elena Park <elena@novamed.ai>

Date: Thu, 01 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Surgeproof sizing, observability checklist & next steps

Jasmine —

Appreciate the analysis and the clear options. A few quick notes from our side:
- We do expect two usage spikes next month tied to a clinical research batch (likely 3x traffic for several 10–20 minute windows).
- Procurement prefers rolling credits rather than expanding the committed GPU count if possible; they asked about price parity and how credits affect SLA.
- SOW: procurement will want line-itemized GPU commit vs burst credits and an ops runbook for failover.

We'll upload the two 24-hour traces by Friday. Please include cost delta examples (monthly) for: (A) +2 GPUs reserved, (B) 15% burst credits, (C) hybrid (buffer + burst) you suggested. Also confirm whether the canary to a quantized variant changes output fidelity checks — we can't have any MRM changes without clinical signoff.

—Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform Engineering, NovaMed AI

Jasmine / Laura —

Forwarding Elena's note. Quick technical take for the sim:
- We'll model three scenarios: +2 reserved GPUs (same model), 15% burst credits routed to quantized variant (Q4/FP16 equiv), and hybrid (2 GPU buffer + 10% burst).
- Metrics to produce: projected monthly token cost, expected P95/P99 latency under the March surge pattern, cache hit-rate sensitivity (we'll vary prefix cache hit from 35% to 80%).
- Canary plan: route 5% traffic for 24 hours to quantized variant with automatic rollback on a fidelity delta > 0.5 BLEU-equivalent or user-defined metric (you specified clinical signoff — we'll add a hard stop there).

I can get the P95/P99 forecasts + cost deltas in ~36 hours once we have the traces. Also flagging an ops ask: we should include the observability checklist items as mandatory deliverables in the SOW (KV cache metrics, per-request trace IDs, token-level cost breakdown). Laura — can you draft the SOW language for the burst-credit line item?

Ben
